# Chicago Education Digest
_Jul 13 – Jul 27, 2026_

> Covering: K-12 Education & Schools · Board of Education & Governance

## K-12 Education & Schools

Chicago Public Schools (CPS) is currently addressing a significant budget shortfall, estimated between $700 million and $732 million. To close this gap, the district has proposed a nearly $10 billion budget that includes laying off 760 teachers and 162 other employees, implementing five furlough days, and enacting a spending freeze. Public hearings have been held on the budget proposal, drawing concerns from Board of Education members and the Chicago Teachers Union (CTU) regarding the proposed cuts and potential layoffs. The district also reported that delayed Cook County tax collections have shorted CPS by $250 million, increasing borrowing costs as the Board prepares for a budget vote and aims to ensure September payroll.

In the context of upcoming school board elections, a notable tension has emerged between staff unions, with the Chicago Teachers Union (CTU) and SEIU endorsing different candidates for school board president and other seats. Separately, the district is addressing a rise in special education needs and associated costs, responding with plans for separate classrooms and increased staffing. This follows an incident where a student with autism reportedly wandered from a CPS summer school camp.

Further developments include a report indicating that over 700 CPS employees were disciplined for misconduct over the past year, with 10 facing allegations of sexual abuse.

## Board of Education & Governance

Chicago Public Schools (CPS) is currently navigating a significant budget deficit, reported to be between $700 million and $732 million, as it prepares its nearly $10 billion budget plan for the upcoming school year. To address this shortfall, the proposed budget includes measures such as the layoff of 760 teachers and other staff, the implementation of five furlough days, and a general spending freeze. These proposals have been the subject of public hearings, where Board of Education members have expressed concerns regarding the potential impact of these cuts. A contributing factor to the deficit includes a reported $250 million shortfall from county property tax collection issues.

Amidst these financial challenges, the governance landscape is also seeing notable activity, particularly concerning the upcoming school board elections. The Chicago Teachers Union (CTU) has been actively rallying against the proposed layoffs and has endorsed candidates in 15 of the 21 school board seats up for election. An emerging tension is the widening rift between major staff unions, with the CTU and SEIU endorsing opposing candidates for school board president. Additionally, one candidate for school board president, Hilario Dominguez, is facing a complaint related to campaign finance rules.
